docs.text:
Matthew Sanderson Datasheet as part of Smart Door Sensor for Team 209

Submission: September, 3, 2025

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: • This datasheet shows the details for Matthew Sanderson's portion of the Auto-Lock Door Sensor.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text:
• Team 209 is a collaborative engineering group dedicated to pushing the boundaries of home security through innovative technology. We aim to design and build an electronic door sensor that automatically locks the door after you close it. This device will provide convenience and security by letting you know your house is safely locked when you leave. Through this project, we seek not only to create a functional and reliable prototype but also to develop as a cohesive team, applying engineering practices and innovative thinking, to deliver a product with real-world impact.
  • The full project website can be viewed here team report.

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text: • My portion of this project was focused on creating a keypad that will control the volume of our speaker as well as stop the alarm when the correct code is entered.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Parts of the block diagram:

  • 8 EK1019 buttons
  • 74HC165 PISO
  • AOT6218L MOSFET
  • Analog 7 input from team
  • Digital 2 output
  • 5V power from PIC Curiosity Nano board

docs.title: 8-Bit Parallel in Serial out (PISO) Shift Register
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons * Option 1.* 74HC165-Q100 surface mount shift register* $0.24/each* link to product * Inexpensive* Directly outputs serial* Meets surface mount constraint of project * Slow shipping speed* Needs special PCB layout * Option 2. * 74HC595D surface mount shift register * $0.63/each * Link to product * Meets surface mount constraint of project * High noise immunity * Directly outputs serial * Exceeding absolute max ratings, even briefly lead to deterioration * Slow shipping speed * Option 3. * SN74HCS165 surface mount shift register * $1.52/each * Link to product * Meets surface mount constraint of project * Wide operating voltage range 2V to 6V * Directly outputs serial * More expensive * Slow shipping speed

Choice: Option 1: 74HC165-Q100 surface mount shift register

Rationale: This shift register is the cheapest option and is not missing any needed features. The added benefits of the more expensive options do not add anything ciritical for this project so do not make sense to choose.

Table 2: Push Button Options

docs.title: Push Button
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons * Option 1.* PTS645 Tactile Switch * $0.28/each* link to product * Inexpensive* Long life expectancy* Taller button * Slow shipping speed * Option 2. * WS-TASV SMT Tact Switch * $0.21/each * Link to product * Meets surface mount constraint of project * Long life expectancy * High quality * Not impact resistant * Slow shipping speed * Difficult to mount * Option 3. * TS34-62-25-BK-100-SMT-TR Tactile Switch * $0.26/each * Link to product * Inexpensive * Long life expectancy * Wide power range * Small button * Slow shipping speed

Choice: Option 1: PTS Tavtile Switch

Rationale: This switch is inexpensive, easy to mount, and has a large enough button.

Table 3: Voltage Regulator Options

docs.title: Voltage Regulator
docs.text:
Solution Pros Cons * Option 1.* AOT2618L TO-220 MOSFET * $1.66/each* link to product * Inexpensive* Meets voltage requirements of project * Low power loss when switching * Slow shipping speed * Option 2. * IPP038N15NM6AKSA1 PG-TO220-3 MOSFET * $5.16/each * Link to product * Meets voltage requirements of project * Superior thermal resistance * Lead free * More expensive * Slow shipping speed * Option 3. * LM7805C TO-220 MOSFET * $1.80/each * Link to product * Meets voltage requirements of project * Easy to use * Internal thermal overload protection * Slow shipping speed

Choice: Option 1: AOT2618L TO-220 MOSFET

Rationale: This voltage regulator is inexpensive, meets the voltage requirements, and we already have it.
